subject: Geofence enforcement & activation windows — RFP clarification
messages:
From: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@atlanticbank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@atlanticbank.com
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -0500
Subject: Geofence enforcement & activation windows — RFP clarification

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the quick availability to support our RFP. A few clarifying questions from our security and operations teams (section 3 of the RFP) so we can complete scoring:

1) Geofence enforcement — please confirm whether customer data (both at-rest and in-transit) is prevented from leaving the customer-selected region (EU) by default for the Hosted offering. If there are exceptions (control plane traffic, logs, cache eviction) please identify what is exempt and how it is controlled/contracted.

2) Backups & DR copies — are backups stored in-region by default? If cross-border replication can occur, what controls/approvals are required and what encryption/locking is applied? Provide RTO/RPO guidance.

3) Activation windows & regional availability — how long does it take to activate an additional region (EU) for a new enterprise tenant in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? Do you offer an SLA for activation or a guaranteed notification window during maintenance or emergency failovers?

4) Proofs — we need a short deliverable for procurement: an evidence bundle we can attach to the RFP (SOC 2 summary, playbook, example activation timeline).

Can you respond with the specifics and attach the evidence bundle? We need this back by COB Monday to hit our committee review.

Appreciate it,

Elaine Turner
Senior Procurement Manager
Atlantic Bank

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@atlanticbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 13:12:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Geofence enforcement & activation windows — RFP clarification

Hi Elaine,

Thanks — and thanks for the clear asks. Below are concise answers and I attached the requested artifacts. If you want, we can also schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with product/infra next week.

1) Geofence enforcement (Hosted):
- Default: Customer data-at-rest (model inputs, outputs, embeddings, logs tied to customer tokens) is stored and encrypted in the customer-selected region (EU) for Hosted accounts that opt into regional residency.
- Control plane metadata: Service control-plane routing metadata (control requests for autoscaling, trigger events) traverses Redwood control plane which is currently multi-region; by default control plane endpoints are registered in the nearest Redwood region and some telemetry may be processed in the US control plane. For customers requiring strict in-region control plane processing we offer a Private deployment or a Control-Plane Geofencing addendum (see playbook).
- Exceptions & controls: Cache eviction keys and short-lived telemetry may be replicated outside the region for performance, but these items are encrypted and do not contain customer prompt content by default. Any egress from a pinned region requires either (a) customer explicit consent via account settings, (b) a contractual exception, or (c) an emergency fallback as defined in the Failover Policy (documented in the playbook).

2) Backups & DR: 
- Hosted: Daily backups are stored in-region by default for EU residency enrollments. Cross-region replication is possible but only with a documented and signed replication policy (customer approval). Backups are AES-256 encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys available for Enterprise/Private.
- RTO/RPO guidance: Typical RTO for Hosted in-region restore: 4–8 hours (standard), RPO: 24 hours. For Dedicated we offer configurable RPO windows down to 1 hour with reserved capacity. Private deployments follow customer DR SLAs and are negotiated.

3) Activation windows & regional availability:
- Hosted (standard account): Enabling an existing Redwood region (e.g., EU-West) for an enrolled tenant: typically completes within 24–72 hours after verification of identity and residency options.
- Hosted (low-touch fast path): For customers who opt into pre-provisioning (annual commitment), activation can be as fast as 6–12 hours during business hours.
- Dedicated: Provisioning reserved capacity in a region usually requires 2–4 weeks (capacity scheduling).
- Private (on-prem/VPC): 4–8 weeks depending on network onboarding and compliance checks.
- Activation SLA/notifications: We provide a notification window for scheduled activations/maintenance of 72 hours by default. For emergency failovers we have a documented failover escalation path and will notify stakeholders within 60 minutes of automatic fallback. The region-activation SLA spreadsheet attached lists guaranteed timelines per tier.

4) Proofs & deliverables: Attached: redwood-geofence-playbook.pdf (detailed controls + exceptions), region-activation-sla.xlsx (timelines per offering), SOC2-summary.pdf. If you need a single-page evidence bundle formatted for your vendor committee, I can produce one.

Summary: For most Hosted EU residency enrollments, customer data remains in-region by default; cross-region moves require explicit approval or a contractual exception. Activation windows vary by offering (6–72 hours for Hosted depending on product path).

Let me know if you want a one-pager for the committee or a product call.

Best,

Mina Haddad
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: redwood-geofence-playbook.pdf (excerpt), region-activation-sla.xlsx, SOC2-summary.pdf]

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: Atlantic Bank asks for binding geofence clause (prep for contract)

Vivek / Marissa,

FYI — Atlantic Bank is asking for a few concrete guarantees to include in the RFP. They want:

1) Single-line answers for procurement (encryption key custody, single RTO number for in-region restore).
2) Clarification on whether emergency cross-region failover requires a contractual exception or whether the default 60-minute notification constitutes consent.

Suggested immediate responses:
- Encryption keys: Hosted EU backups use Redwood-managed keys by default; customer-managed keys (CMKs) via KMS are available for Enterprise customers and are documented in the SOC2 summary.
- In-region RTO: 6 hours (target for hosted in-region restore, standard offering).
- Emergency failover: Emergency cross-region failover is considered a last-resort operational action; it will only occur under our documented Failover Policy and requires notification within 60 minutes and a post-incident review. Any right to automatic cross-region failover without customer approval must be added as an explicit contractual exception.

Action: Marissa — can you draft a short clause for the Data Residency Addendum that codifies the above and includes an option for CMK? Vivek — please confirm the 6-hour RTO is acceptable from Ops side or propose an alternate number. I want to send back a one-paragraph answer and the clause draft to Elaine by COB today (their timeline slipped and they want this).

Thanks,

Mina Haddad
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
